$comment: The weekly scouring brief: where to look for novel AI use cases in the workplace, what counts as one, and how to score a find before it becomes a post. Run one pass a week. Nothing publishable is a normal outcome - the disqualifiers exist so the account does not fill with product news.
what_we_are_looking_for: A specific instance of somebody's actual job being done differently. A named function, a before and after in the work itself, and enough detail that a manager in a different industry could recognise their own version of it. The nuggets in nuggets.json are the matching set: a find is worth writing about when it is a concrete case of one of those claims, or a genuine counterexample to one.

novelty_test.$comment: All five have to hold. Any one of them missing and it is product news, not a use case.
novelty_test.named_function: You can say which job it is. Claims adjuster, ward pharmacist, dispatcher, grant writer, line cook. Not 'knowledge workers'.
novelty_test.the_work_changed: Something about how the work is done is different, not just which tool is open. If the answer is 'they use a chatbot now', keep reading.
novelty_test.a_person_decided: Somebody made a call about scope, boundaries or supervision, and you can say what the call was.
novelty_test.checkable_detail: At least one specific that could be wrong: a threshold, a step that got removed, a rule, a number of cases, a handoff.
novelty_test.transferable: A manager in an unrelated field would recognise the structure of the problem.

disqualifiers: A model release, a benchmark score, or a funding round.
A vendor case study with results and no process. If it does not say what the agent was not allowed to do, there is no post in it.
An anonymous 'a Fortune 500 company' with no function named.
A pilot with no described supervision. Pilots that nobody checked are not use cases, they are announcements.
Anything under 48 hours old where the facts are still moving.

scoring.$comment: Score a candidate 0-3 on each. Six or better is worth drafting; anything with a 0 on specificity gets dropped regardless of total.
scoring.specificity: How concrete is the detail. 3 means you could describe the process to someone who does that job and they would nod.
scoring.spine_fit: Does it carry one of the four spine themes without being bent to fit. 3 means the story is already about that.
scoring.recognisability: Would the audience see their own week in it. 3 means they have had the same argument in their own function.
scoring.honesty_headroom: Is there a real counterpoint you can include without wrecking the post. 3 means the story has a genuine cost or tradeoff in it, which is what makes it credible.
scoring.freshness: Not staleness, but whether the account has said this recently. 3 means the angle has not appeared in the last eight posts.

sources.name: Peer-reviewed and working-paper economics of AI at work
sources.good_for: Task-level rather than job-level findings, which is the altitude this account argues at.
sources.watch_for: Preprints without review. Say 'a working paper reports' and mean it.

sources.name: Management press
sources.good_for: The management framing this account shares, and named operational frameworks worth arguing with.
sources.watch_for: Consulting content marketing wearing a journal's typeface.

sources.name: Industry trade press
examples: Modern Healthcare and Becker's for hospitals
Legal Tech News and Law360 for legal
sources.good_for: The richest vein by far. Trade press writes for practitioners, so it names the function and the process instead of the vendor.

sources.name: Regulators, auditors and standards bodies
examples: NIST AI Risk Management Framework updates
state and national labour and health regulators
sources.good_for: Accountability and supervision material - the performance-review and named-supervisor nuggets. Audit reports in particular describe what actually happened, in detail, under oath.
sources.watch_for: Draft guidance read as if it were in force.

sources.name: Practitioner communities
examples: subreddits for specific trades and professions
conference talks by people who run the function
sources.good_for: The unglamorous detail nobody publishes: the workaround, the rule they added after the incident, the thing they turned off.
sources.watch_for: Single anonymous accounts. Corroborate before quoting, and never quote a named individual without their public consent.

sources.name: Labour market data
sources.good_for: Evidence about whether roles like agent manager are actually being hired, which is the weak point in the six-capabilities nugget.
sources.watch_for: Job title inflation. A posting is an intention, not a job.

queries.$comment: Starting points for a weekly search pass. Rotate rather than running all of them - the aim is one good find, not a survey.
structural: "agent manager" job description line of business
who owns AI agents org chart "not IT"
AI agent "escalate to a human" threshold policy
"human in the loop" removed OR added after incident
by_function: AI workflow nurses scheduling hospital rollout what changed
claims adjusters AI triage rules exceptions
public sector caseworker AI pilot evaluation report
counterexample: AI pilot rolled back reason process
"we turned it off" AI tool team workflow
queries.note: The counterexample queries earn their place. A find that contradicts a nugget is more valuable than a fifth confirmation of one, and it is the only reliable way to keep the account from becoming a fan account for its own thesis.

candidate_schema.$comment: What to record for a find, whether or not it becomes a post. Kept so the same story does not get rediscovered every six weeks.
candidate_schema.source_url: the primary source, not an aggregator's rewrite of it
candidate_schema.what_changed: one sentence on the work before and after
candidate_schema.the_decision: the scope, boundary or supervision call somebody made
candidate_schema.nuggets: which claims it instantiates or contradicts
candidate_schema.verdict: draft, hold, or drop, with one line of reasoning

workflow: 1. Read the nuggets first. You are looking for instances, not for interesting news.
2. Run two or three queries, including one counterexample query.
3. Apply the novelty test before reading anything closely. It kills most items in a sentence.
4. Score what survives. Record every candidate, including the drops.
5. Take the best one to a draft. If nothing scores six, publish from the queue instead and say nothing about it - a quiet week is not a content emergency.
6. Before drafting, check the last eight posts for the same angle.

network_allowlist.$comment: A scouring pass needs to open primaries, not just search titles. In a sandboxed session outbound access is allowlisted, so a pass that cannot fetch stops at triage and every candidate stays at 'hold'. Paste this list into the environment's Custom network access allowlist to let a pass finish. Search still works at any access level.
network_allowlist.note: Keep it to publishers and institutions the brief already names. A wide-open allowlist is not the goal; being able to read the source you are about to quote is.
